overview.description: Hoola (or Hulla) is a popular Korean rummy game related to the Japanese game Seven Bridge. It is a fast-paced game of sets and runs, where the goal is to empty your hand. It features unique mechanics like 'Blasts' (winning with specific sevens) and 'Knocking' (claiming a win when your point total is low).

history.origins: Likely developed in the late 20th century as an evolution of Western and Japanese Rummy variants (specifically Seven Bridge). It became a dominant social game in Korea.
timeline: 1980s: Hoola emerges in Korean gathering places.
1990s: Rules stabilize into the 'Battle Hoola' format.
Present: One of the most common casual card games in Korea, with many mobile versions.
history.evolution: The game evolved from a standard 'draw and discard' rummy into a more aggressive version where players can 'battle' for the discard.
history.cultural: Commonly played as a social 'filler' game or for small stakes (e.g., in PC bangs or among friends).

setup.dealing: Deal 7 cards to each player (anticlockwise). The remaining cards form the stock.

rules.objective: Win by melding all cards in your hand or having the lowest point total when someone 'knocks'.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players draw from the stock or claim the discard.
2. **Battle**: If multiple players want the discard, there is a priority system (usually the next player in order has first right).
3. **Melding**: - **Sets**: 3 or 4 cards of the same rank. - **Runs**: 3+ consecutive cards of the same suit (Cyclic: K-A-2 is allowed). - **Sevens**: A single 7 can be melded alone.
4. **Blast**: Winning with a specific combination involving 7s or a clean sweep of the hand recorded as a 'Blast' (double points).
keyRules: Follow the legal action constraints defined for Hoola.
Round outcome is resolved by the scoring method: - Face cards: 10-13 pts.
Winning condition: Win by melding all cards in your hand or having the lowest point total when someone 'knocks'.

strategy.basic: Prioritize melding your high cards (Kings, Queens) first to reduce your point total in case someone else wins.
strategy.intermediate: Keep a 7 in your hand until you can use it to 'close' out a hand or as a safe exit. Melding a 7 alone is a good way to reduce your count.
strategy.advanced: The 'Battle' strategy: Don't just take the discard because you need it; take it to prevent an opponent from matching it if they are close to emptying their hand.
tips: Watch the discard pile; in Hoola, cards can turn the corner (K-A-2), making Aces very flexible.
If you have a 7, remember it's a 'double penalty' (14 pts) if it stays in your hand.

list.name: Hoola without Battles
list.description: Discard can only be taken when it is your turn; if multiple want it, the player whose turn is earlier gets it. Or play non-battle: only the player to your left's discard can be taken, on your turn.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Rule change only; no engine overrides needed for turn-order variant.

list.name: Six or Seven Players
list.description: With 6 or 7 players, one or two drop out after the deal so exactly five play. Dealer cannot drop out; forced drop-outs may claim compensation for sevens, sets or sequences.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Player count and drop-out rules; overrides to be added when supported.

list.name: Hoola Multiplier
list.description: Some play that the multiplier for going out with a Perfect (all 7 cards melded at once) is only double, not quadruple.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes multiplier constant; no engine overrides identified yet.

drawSources.notes: Draw one from stock at start of turn.
Only if used immediately in a new three-card meld; Battle Hoola allows claim out of turn.

discardPickRules.frozenPileRules: Only to form new three-card meld; not to add to existing meld or keep in hand.

meldConfig.initialMeldRequirement: Three equal cards, three consecutive same suit, or a single Seven. May add to existing melds only after having played a complete new meld.

goingOut.condition: Meld all cards; or knock with 10 or fewer deadwood (7s count 14); or blast (15 or fewer or 83+ unmelded at start of turn); or four sevens in hand; or stock exhausted.

edgeCases.text: If knocker is tied or undercut on points, knocker ranks last and pays all losers' stakes to winner.
The player who discarded the card that was claimed and used to go out ranks last and pays all losers' stakes to winner.
Player with four sevens in hand may stop and win immediately.
At start of turn with no melds yet, 15 or fewer or 83+ points (7s count 7) allows stopping and winning (Sopang/Daepang).
Player who has melded nothing when another wins ranks last; payment may be doubled.
Each unmelded Seven at end doubles that player's payment to winner.

customActions.description: Draw one card from the top of the stock pile. Compulsory at start of turn unless claiming the discard to form a new meld.
customActions.constraints: Allowed only in phases that list this action as legal.

customActions.description: Take the top card of the discard pile to form a new three-card meld from hand; in Battle Hoola may claim out of turn. Card must be used immediately in the new meld.
customActions.constraints: Only legal if the card is used immediately in a new three-card meld (set, run, or with a Seven).

customActions.description: End the round when your deadwood is 10 points or fewer (sevens count 14). All show hands; lowest total wins. If tied or undercut, knocker ranks last.
customActions.constraints: Only at start of turn; deadwood must be 10 or fewer.

customActions.description: Resolve round: rank players by deadwood (7s count 14), apply payments and penalties, then continue to next round or end game.
customActions.constraints: System-only; allowed only in round_end phase.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck with four suits and thirteen ranks per suit; no jokers. Used for Hoola (Korean rummy), where players form melds (sets and runs) and knock when their deadwood is low enough.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each contain thirteen cards. Melds are three or more of the same rank (sets) or three or more in sequence in the same suit (runs).
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks Ace through King; Ace may be high or low in runs. Face cards count 10 points for deadwood; Aces 1; number cards face value. The goal is to meld and knock with minimal deadwood.
engine.dealPattern: One card at a time to each player anticlockwise until each has 7 cards. Next card face up for discard; remainder form stock.

scoring.description: Players score points for cards in hand. Melding reduces point total. First to meld all cards or lowest total when knocked wins.
scoring.winCondition: Empty hand first, or lowest point total when someone knocks.
